title: Printable symmetry grids and star sheet (lesson 66)
subject: Mathematics
source: Seeded from mathematics/y8 lesson 66 (Printable symmetry grids and star sheet (portal worksheet for this lesson; usable on a drawing tablet))
intro: Lesson 66: Line and rotational symmetry. To understand how to find the lines of symmetry and the order of rotational symmetry of 2D shapes and patterns

questions.q: Give the lines of symmetry and the order of rotational symmetry of a rhombus.
questions.model: The two diagonals are fold lines (the halves match). It fits onto itself after a half turn and a full turn: order 2.

questions.q: (a) Give the lines of symmetry and the order for: an isosceles triangle, a rectangle, a regular 10-gon, an isosceles trapezium. (b) On the 4 by 4 printable grid, shade squares to make a pattern with exactly 2 lines of symmetry and order 2. (c) Sketch a shape with order 3 but no lines of symmetry.
questions.a: (a) 1 and 1; 2 and 2; 10 and 10; 1 and 1 (b) for example a 2 by 4 block shaded across the middle of the grid (c) for example a three-armed pinwheel
questions.model: (a) Isosceles triangle: one fold line from the top angle to the middle of the base; it only fits onto itself after a full turn, so order 1.

questions.q: On the printable star sheet, shade a pattern with order 6 and 6 lines of symmetry, and another with order 6 and no lines.
questions.a: Teacher checks: for no lines, use swirl (pinwheel) shading that keeps the turns.

questions.q: A regular polygon has rotational symmetry of order 9. How many lines of symmetry has it, and what is its exterior angle?
The order of rotational symmetry of a square is:
Lines of symmetry of a regular hexagon
Big question: how many ways can a shape fit onto itself?
questions.a: As many as its order of rotational symmetry; a regular n-gon fits n ways by turning and also has n fold lines.
